newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bufete Q2 forecasted loss sans extra sale.
newsitem.headline: Bufete Q2 forecasted loss sans extra sale.

text.p: Mexican builder Bufete Industrial should see its year-ago loss reversed when it presents second quarter earnings results, but only because of an extraordinary item, analysts said.

Analysts said the sale of its Mexpetrol stake for $33 million gave a boost in profits. Four analysts surveyed by Reuters saw an average earnings per share of 3.52 pesos, compared with a 0.53 peso loss in the second quarter of 1996.
"The profit that will be reported is because of Mexpetrol. If we remove this, they would show a loss of 0.26 pesos per share," BBV-Probursa analyst Monica Lourdes de Leon said.

Industry observers forecast Bufete's second quarter sales at 937.7 million pesos, a real fall of 8.52 percent from the year-ago period. Operating profits were seen up 10 percent for the second quarter of 1997, at 39.6 million pesos.
Income weakness was due to the absence of new contracts in the second quarter, Serfin brokerage analyst Gerardo Saenz said in a report.
Operating margins fell to 4.3 percent from 4.4 percent in the first quarter, but were above 3.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996, he added.

"(The improvement in margins) is because of the good control over general administrative and sales expenses, and the projects that are now being carried out have a better margin," Caspian Securities analyst Sebastian Chatel said.
Analysts said that Bufete's near future will be tied to its return on projects with the Federal Electricity Commission, such as the Carbon II and Topolobampo generators.
One tripping point in the earnings report could be Bufete's backlog, which analysts said may have fallen about 20 percent from the first quarter's $367 million.
The backlog was seen improving in the second half of the year, depending on how Bufete fares in megaprojects being auctioned by state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).

Still, some analysts said Bufete could be betting too much on the two contracts it is vying for, a $1.2 billion expansion of the Cadereyta refinery and the $1 billion construction of a nitrogen plant at the Cantarell oil field.
These megaprojects offer more attractive margins than smaller contracts, analysts said.

"If they do not take (the megaprojects), they will have to enter the smaller contests that don't provide very attractive margins, because Bufete is not in conditions to make aggressive bids," UBS Securities Alvaro Shiraishi said.
